rationale: Manichaean technical term for the fifth and lowest of the food-offspring: the procreative child fashioned in the flesh through sexual desire. ⲝⲡⲟ = ϫⲡⲟ 'beget' + Greek σωματικόν 'bodily.' Distinct from the four pneumatic/exudative offspring (breath, speech, sweat, sexual emission).

First of the five food-offspring; rises from the body through breath and mounts upon the mind. Likely related to ⲡⲱϣⲙ 'breath, exhalation' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲱϣⲙⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'fragrant-breath'). Lyc. orthographic variant.
Used of the third food-offspring emerging through 'power and shame' (sweat? other bodily exudate). Possibly reduplicated form on a pouring/exuding root. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Privative ⲁⲧ- + ⲉⲓⲃⲉ 'thirst' = 'without thirst' = unfailing/inexhaustible. Modifies ⲥⲕⲉⲟⲥ 'vessel' in the eschatological pearl-and-vessel imagery. Distinct from accumulated ⲁⲧⲉⲓⲃⲉ 'without number' (different context).

proposed_english: the second / the third / the fourth / the fifth (masc. ordinal series)
rationale: Lycopolitan masculine ordinal series ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩ-N parallel to the feminine ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍ-N already attested in glossary. Applied here to enumerate the five food-offspring.
Greek loanword αἰσθάνομαι 'perceive, sense' with Coptic verbalizing prefix ⲣ-. Standard sensory-cognitive verb. Used here in negation: 'they do not perceive the other four offspring.'
